extracted.intended_audience: litigation counsel, data protection officers, judges, and parties handling cross-border discovery/ESI
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and model orders for managing preservation, production, transfer, and protection of Protected Data in cross-border civil litigation, reconciling U.S. discovery obligations with foreign Data Protection Laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle 1 — Respect for foreign Data Protection Laws and Data Subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: With regard to data that is subject to preservation, disclosure, or discovery in a U.S. legal proceeding, courts and parties should demonstrate due respect to the Data Protection Laws of any foreign sovereign and the interests of any person who is subject to or benefits from such laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General admonition that U.S. discovery actors should account for and defer to foreign data protection interests when possible; forms the baseline obligation guiding other principles and procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle 2 — Good faith and reasonableness when conflicts arise
rubrics_metrics.description: Where full compliance with both Data Protection Laws and preservation, disclosure, and discovery obligations presents a conflict, a party’s conduct should be judged by a court or data protection authority under a standard of good faith and reasonableness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides evaluative standard for party conduct facing conflicting obligations: courts/authorities should assess whether parties acted reasonably and in good faith rather than imposing strict liability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle 3 — Limit preservation, disclosure, and discovery to relevant and necessary data
rubrics_metrics.description: Preservation, disclosure, and discovery of Protected Data should be limited in scope to that which is relevant and necessary to support any party’s claim or defense in order to minimize conflicts of law and impact on the Data Subject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overarching requirement to minimize intrusion into Protected Data; anticipates use of narrowing techniques and proportionality analyses to reduce cross-border conflict and privacy impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle 3.A — Limit the Scope of the Request
rubrics_metrics.description: Limit the scope of requests for Protected Data so that discovery seeks only what is relevant and necessary and thereby minimizes conflict with Data Protection Laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages targeted requests, narrowing by subject matter, time, custodians, and data types; ties to proportionality and relevance concepts in Rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle 3.B — Discovery with Specificity
rubrics_metrics.description: Discovery requests should be sufficiently specific to allow meaningful assessment of relevance and proportionality and to enable targeted protection of Protected Data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A specific request reduces fishing expeditions and facilitates negotiations over protective measures or limitation of production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle 3.C — Phased Discovery
rubrics_metrics.description: Use phased discovery to limit early production to the most critical, narrowly-defined materials and defer broader requests until necessity is demonstrated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Phasing can reduce unnecessary transfer/processing of Protected Data and allow iterative narrowing based on initial results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle 3.D — Minimize the Production of Protected Data
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties should minimize the amount of Protected Data produced by using culling, de-duplication, targeted searches, and other narrowing techniques.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical measures include questionnaires, interviews, technology-assisted review, country-level compilation, and producing non-protected equivalents where available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle 3.E — Substitution of Data
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider substituting non-protected data or redacted versions in lieu of full Protected Data when appropriate to satisfy discovery needs while protecting privacy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substitution (e.g., redaction, synthetic or aggregated datasets, summaries) reduces the need to transfer protected personal data and can be part of agreed protocols or court orders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle 3.F — Limitations on the Format of Production
rubrics_metrics.description: Limit the format of production (e.g., native files, image files, metadata included) to what is necessary, to avoid unnecessary disclosure of Protected Data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prescribe formats that mitigate privacy exposure (e.g., exclude non-essential metadata, produce redacted images rather than native files when metadata contains sensitive data).

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle 4 — Use stipulation or court order to protect Protected Data
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a conflict exists between Data Protection Laws and preservation, disclosure, or discovery obligations, a stipulation or court order should be employed to protect Protected Data and minimize the conflict.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages parties to obtain protective orders, stipulations, or court directives that explicitly address cross-border protections and limitations on use and dissemination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle 4.A — Protective Order or Stipulation (model protective order)
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ a protective order or stipulation (for example, the Model U.S. Federal Court Protective Order in Appendix C) that combines conventional confidentiality restrictions with additional protections for classes of information (e.g., personal information) because of international and domestic Data Protection Laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Model protective order includes designations (Confidential/Highly Confidential), permitted uses, Authorized Recipient rules, data security requirements, breach notification, and end-of-matter disposition procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle 4.B — Scheduling Stipulation or Order
rubrics_metrics.description: Use scheduling stipulations or orders to sequence preservation, collection, review, and production activities to minimize unnecessary processing/transfers of Protected Data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scheduling can implement phased discovery and allow time for legal, regulatory, or compliance steps (e.g., consultations with Data Protection Authorities) before transfer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle 4.C — Legitimization Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare a legitimization plan explaining and documenting the legal bases and safeguards used to justify transfers of Protected Data (e.g., Model Contracts, Privacy Shield, Binding Corporate Rules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A plan documents transfer mechanisms, contractual safeguards, and other legal bases to present to courts or data protection authorities and to support good faith compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle 5 — Data Controller must demonstrate addressed data protection obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: A Data Controller subject to preservation, disclosure, or discovery obligations should be prepared to demonstrate that data protection obligations have been addressed and that appropriate data protection safeguards have been instituted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expectation that Data Controllers keep records and evidence of steps taken (e.g., risk assessments, technical measures, consultations) and be able to show compliance to courts or authorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle 6 — Retention limited to necessity; preserve relevant information with safeguards
rubrics_metrics.description: Data Controllers should retain Protected Data only as long as necessary to satisfy legal or business needs. While a legal action is pending or remains reasonably anticipated, Data Controllers should preserve relevant information, including relevant Protected Data, with appropriate data safeguards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balances preservation duties against over-retention; emphasizes reasonable, proportionate preservation and secure handling while litigation is pending or anticipated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of discovery under Fed. R. Civ. P. (relevance, proportionality, burden)
rubrics_metrics.description: Discovery must be relevant to a party’s claim or defense and proportional to the needs of the case; it should not be cumulative or duplicative and should be sought from the most convenient, least burdensome, and least expensive source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites Fed. R. Civ. P. 26(b)(1) and 26(b)(2)(C); courts must consider importance of issues, amount in controversy, parties’ access to information, resources, and whether burden outweighs benefit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to preserve: trigger and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: The duty to preserve arises when a party first learns of the litigation or should have reasonably anticipated it; it does not require preservation of every possible piece of data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preservation requires reasonable steps to maintain relevant information; excessive preservation is discouraged (rule amendments and case law recognize reasonable steps suffice); sanctions are available for improper destruction but preservation obligations are not limitless.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judicial balancing for cross-border production (comity and factors)
rubrics_metrics.description: U.S. courts may order production of information located outside the U.S. or restricted by foreign law, but must weigh multiple factors (as guided by U.S. Supreme Court precedents) to determine whether to exercise that authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Being subject to civil, administrative, or criminal sanctions abroad is a factor but not dispositive; courts weigh comity, importance of the evidence, privacy laws, and other considerations when compelling cross-border production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model Protective Order — Designation and permitted use restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Confidential Material and Highly Confidential Material may be designated, and such designations restrict use to the litigation and forbid other uses or dissemination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Model Order sets definitions for categories, prohibits use for competitive purpose, requires Authorized Recipients, sets limits on copying and transcription, and includes provisions for challenging designations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model Protective Order — Authorized Recipients and access limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Limit access to Protected Data to Authorized Recipients (e.g., outside and in-house counsel, experts, witnesses under certain conditions) and impose obligations on those recipients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorized Recipients must execute acknowledgments (see Exhibit A), be bound by the order, and are limited in how they may use or disclose the data; special rules may apply for vendors and third-party service providers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model Protective Order — Information security program and technical safeguards
rubrics_metrics.description: A party in possession of Confidential or Highly Confidential Material shall maintain a written information security program including reasonable administrative, technical, and physical safeguards to protect such material against anticipated threats and unauthorized access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minimum standards are specified and may include encryption in transit and at rest, SFTP/SSL/VPN use, controlled access, vendor due diligence, background checks, and incident response procedures; vendors may be used if they maintain comparable programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model Protective Order — Breach notification, investigation, and remediation
rubrics_metrics.description: If a Receiving Party or Authorized Recipient discovers any loss or breach of Confidential or Highly Confidential Material, they must promptly notify the Disclosing Party, investigate and remediate, provide assurances that recurrence will be prevented, and cooperate with investigations and law enforcement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires prompt written notice, reasonable remediation efforts, cooperation in investigation, and provision of information sufficient for the Disclosing Party to assess scope and impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model Protective Order — End-of-matter data disposition
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon final resolution of the litigation the Parties will certify that all Confidential Material and/or Highly Confidential Material has been returned to the Producing Party and/or securely destroyed as agreed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order contemplates insertion of specific return/destroy procedures and requires certification; parties should negotiate or court should order appropriate end-of-matter disposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model Protective Order — Remedies for violations and court retention of jurisdiction
rubrics_metrics.description: If any person or party violates the Protective Order, the aggrieved Disclosing Party may apply to the Court for relief, including injunctive relief at the court’s discretion; the Court retains jurisdiction to enforce the order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard enforcement mechanisms include motion practice and injunctive relief; the model preserves courts' remedial powers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exhibit A — Acknowledgment of Protected Data restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuals receiving Protected Data must acknowledge receipt of the Protective Order, agree to comply with its terms (including data security and end-of-matter obligations), and submit to the Court’s jurisdiction for enforcement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form acknowledgment collects name, employer, address, signature, and affirms understanding and submission to court jurisdiction for enforcement purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protocol Instruction 1 — Explain reasons and identify proceeding
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain the reasons for preserving or collecting the data and identify clearly the U.S. proceeding (active or reasonably anticipated) for which the Protected Data is processed and transferred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include case name, docket number, filing location, filing date, and description of the proceeding; this grounds the Protocol and demonstrates purpose to data protection authorities or courts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protocol Instruction 2 — Determine applicable Data Protection Laws and sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether data required to be preserved, processed, or disclosed in the U.S. is subject to Data Protection Laws and, if so, which laws apply; assess whether alternative, non-protected sources exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify the relevant national laws, locations of data, sources of Protected Data, and whether non-protected equivalents can be produced to avoid transferring protected information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protocol Instruction 3 — Describe measures to minimize processing and transfers
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe measures taken to minimize the processing and transfer of Protected Data, including methodologies used to filter and eliminate irrelevant Protected Data (culling, interviews, iterative software tools).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May include collecting data locally or in a country not subject to transfer restrictions, use of questionnaires and iterative ESI searches, de-duplication, and technology-assisted review to create a limited subset for disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protocol Instruction 4 — Identify categories of Protected Data
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the various categories of Protected Data that will be processed or transferred by type (personal and sensitive personal data, trade secrets, restricted data, consumer data, state secrets, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Categorization assists in tailoring protections, redactions, and choosing transfer legitimization mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protocol Instruction 5 — Limitations on use and dissemination
rubrics_metrics.description: If appropriate, use model protective orders or stipulations that impose agreed-upon restrictions on the use, disclosure, and dissemination of Protected Data (including redaction and Confidential/Highly Confidential designations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider restrictions on onward transfer, limitations to litigation use, and other constraints to satisfy Data Protection requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protocol Instruction 6 — Transparency to Data Subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Strive to provide a transparent processing and transfer protocol to Data Subjects, identifying impacted Data Subjects and communicating purpose, categories of data, duties, protections, and methods of contact or consent where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communications can include postings, meetings, notice and acknowledgement documentation, and should be provided in English and the local language where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protocol Instruction 7 — Steps to secure transferred Protected Data
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify steps taken to secure Protected Data including contractual agreements with third parties, use of protective orders, type of encryption at rest and in transit, and limitations on access and onward transfer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also describe incident response/procedures for breaches and vendor controls; include specifics such as encryption protocols and access management where feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protocol Instruction 8 — Compliance with notification obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe efforts undertaken where notice to oversight bodies or internal stakeholders (data protection officers, works councils, data protection authorities) is contemplated or required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify who was consulted, the nature of consultation, and the manner and timing of any notifications to authorities or internal governance bodies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protocol Instruction 9 — Identify legitimization mechanisms for transfer
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify mechanism(s) used to legitimize transfer of Protected Data (e.g., Binding Corporate Rules, EU/U.S. Privacy Shield certification, EU Model Contract Clauses, or other means).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify the mechanism relied on for each U.S. recipient and document how it applies to the transfer circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protocol Instruction 10 — Disposition procedures for transferred data
rubrics_metrics.description: Document procedures used to destroy or return Protected Data to the Data Controller when it is no longer necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide specific mechanics and timelines for secure destruction or return, and include certification requirements to close the matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protocol Instruction 11 — Identify responsible persons and signatures
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify individuals responsible for overseeing preservation, processing, and transfer of Protected Data and obtain their signatures to signify that the recorded steps were taken.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Having accountable signatories builds a record of good faith compliance and provides points of contact for authorities or courts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protocol Action Item Table — Structured documentation of actions and information
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the Protocol's action-item table to document purpose, laws at issue, minimization measures, categories of data, limitations on use, transparency steps, security measures, notification compliance, transfer bases, disposition, and responsible persons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The table provides an ease-of-reference checklist and creates a record to present to regulators or courts showing steps taken to maximize compliance; must be customized to case facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimization techniques and iterative methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ a combination of interviews/questionnaires, iterative use of software tools, de-duplication, and filtering to create a narrowed subset of relevant and necessary Protected Data for disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly document methodology for culling and filtering to demonstrate efforts to minimize the transferred dataset; consider local compilation to avoid cross-border transfer where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of alternative sources and substitution
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether non-protected sources of relevant data exist and, to the extent possible, produce non-protected sources to reduce need for Protected Data transfers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use substitution (e.g., summaries, redactions, substituted records) as a mitigation; document why substituted materials suffice for discovery needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of third-party vendors under security requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Where parties lack internal information security programs, they may satisfy security requirements by using eDiscovery vendors or claims administrators that maintain appropriate information security programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure vendors maintain comparable written information security programs; include contractual safeguards and audit/assurance measures where appropriate.
